title: OSKA guardrail catalog
description: The governed catalog of guardrails of one installation: every rule the installation promises to keep, declared once and referenced from a skill by identifier. Each entry says where the promise acts and which of the three mechanisms keeps it — a check the guardrail chain runs, an invariant a named module keeps, or an instruction handed to a model — so neither a sentence handed to a model nor a rule kept elsewhere can be read as a control at the point it is declared.

$comment.description: Prose for a reader of the file. Nothing reads it.

guardrails.description: The declared guardrails, keyed by identifier. An identifier a skill names and this object does not define is an error.

title.description: The promise in one line, as a reviewer would state it.

description.description: The promise in full. For an entry acting at the input or the output point this is also the wording the runtime answers in when the guardrail refuses a turn, so it is written to be read by the person who typed the request.

enforcement.description: Where the promise acts and what keeps it. A `check` runs in the guardrail chain at its point, names a validator the runtime registers, and carries every value that validator reads. An `invariant` is kept by the module it names, at a point the chain runs nothing, and carries neither a validator nor parameters. An `instruction` carries neither either, and is never reported as enforcement.

point.description: The point of the turn at which this entry acts. `input` runs before the turn is classified and `output` before the reply is returned; those two are the points the guardrail chain runs. `planning` and `execution` are points it does not run, so a promise acting there is kept by a module and declared as an invariant.

mechanism.description: `check` is code the guardrail chain runs at this point and that can refuse or redact; `invariant` is a promise the named module keeps at a point the chain runs nothing; `instruction` is text handed to a model, which nothing enforces.

validator.description: The registered check that keeps this promise. Required for `check`, forbidden for `invariant` and for `instruction`. A validator the runtime does not register is an error when this file is read.

module.description: Where the promise is kept, so a reader can go and see. For an `invariant` this is the whole of what the entry says about how it is kept.

parameters.description: Everything the validator reads — pattern, set, threshold or word list — carried by the entry rather than written into the code that runs it. Only a `check` has a validator to read them, so only a `check` declares them.

reason.description: What the refusal says, in the words of this entry.
